claims.text: The brief's Swiss stack has seven layers with a table rendering each: 1864 Zeitreihen (old survey under the modern sheet: 'the ruined map'), Building register (every structure: 'a homestead is a dot with a name, not a town icon'), Transit stops (halts as a network: 'the only places a shield is earned'), Marked paths ('the path the party can follow without a guide'), Schiessanzeigen (hazard that turns on and off: 'swap between sessions'), Closures ('the road they expect is shut this week'), Color base map ('contours first, names second').

Stack order is fixed by the brief: Planning locks 'the 1864 sheet under the live one' and puts closures and range notices on top, swappable between sessions; Implementation draws relief first, then water, coast road, reserves, homestead dots, names and heights, then the city, and builds the overlays as separate sheets (old survey, structures, coach posts, blazed paths, range days, closures).

Swap semantics derived from c02 and rulings R12/R14: BASE = colour base (the modern PatrinorModern.png pyramid plus a relief bake from the DEM); UNDER = old survey (R14: an era tile layer stacked under the live base with opacity or swipe, plus an old-name layer if the eras differ only in names); OVER, static and seeded = every structure, caravan halts, blazed paths; OVER, swappable per session = muster days and shut ways, loaded from a notices file or notices=<url> (R12, player-facing label 'the herald's tidings'). Putting structures, halts and paths in the static group is an inference: the brief makes only the closures and range notices swappable.

evidence.ref: docs/filigree/README.md#9 Owner rulings R12, R14; brief p5

claims.text: Fiction names (R10 plus dossier §5): 1864 Zeitreihen -> the old survey (the Imperial sheet, golden age; the War sheet, War of the Patrons 1124-1133); Building register -> every structure (steadings and folds: herders' folds, granaries, wayside Kembar shrines, wells, ruined towers); Transit stops -> caravan halts / waystations (also ferry stairs, fords, cog landings, beacon posts), never 'coach posts'; Marked paths -> blazed paths (cairned ways, drove-tracks, shrine-paths); Schiessanzeigen -> muster days ('artillery hours' and live-fire 'range' wording dropped); Closures -> shut ways; Color base -> PatrinorModern.png era pyramid.

Vocabulary conflict: dossier §5 still says 'Drop it and use "range days"' for Schiessanzeigen, but R10 drops the live-fire 'range' wording and names the layer muster days. R10 governs, so the bible must not carry 'range days' through any more than 'coach posts'.

Old survey today is a swap, not an under-stack. BASES holds three makeBase pyramids (modern 'tiles/', war 'tiles-war/', imperial 'tiles-imperial/', each z0-5 with 860 files). setEra(k) calls removeLayer(curBase) and then addTo the new one, so only one era is ever on the map. The era radios read 'Modern (1374 A.B.)', 'War of the Patrons (1124–1133)' and 'Imperial (the golden age)'.

evidence.ref: maps-site/index.html :: function setEra (826); var BASES= (819-822); name="era" (3332-3334); find maps-site/tiles* -type f | wc -l

claims.text: The era is not in the URL. handleHash parses only journey=, chart=/poi=, company=, faction=, place= and view=, so neither the old-survey state nor an overlay set survives a deep link today. The only split/swipe precedent is prototypes/atlas-night.html, where #mapB is clipped to the right half with clip-path:inset(0 0 0 50%).

On the three old-survey fixture tiles, the war and imperial z5 tiles differ from modern in 69-156 of 65536 pixels (grey diff >30): under 0.25%, scattered across each tile. The eras are near-identical prints with sparse local edits, so an under-layer at partial opacity will show little unless a swipe or an old-name layer (R14) carries the difference.

evidence.ref: PIL ImageChops.difference on maps-site/tiles{,-war,-imperial}/5/{11/11,9/11,10/12}.jpg, threshold 30: war 129/156/115, imperial 72/69/95 px

claims.text: Every structure today exists only inside settlement plans. genCityCanvas is seeded per name (xmur3(name) -> mulberry32) and adds POIs with prov:'invented'. There are no open-country structure records. Atlas data has gazetteer kinds village 13, town 3, ruin 1 (Settlements 131) and 136 city-anchors, so every homestead dot on a sheet would be new, seeded and prov:'invented'.

evidence.ref: maps-site/index.html :: function genCityCanvas (2166-2170), function addPoi (2791); maps-site/data/gazetteer.json#kind counts; maps-site/data/city-anchors.json length

claims.text: Caravan halts must reuse the shipped POI 'The Beacon Post' ('A tarred beacon on its post, unlit in living memory — kept ready all the same.') and must not duplicate it. It is one of 8 entries in the 'odd' pool that genCityCanvas draws for every settlement plan with a uniform pick, so it is an in-town landmark that appears in about 1 in 8 plans, not a network node. The halt layer can cite it where it rolls, but the halt network itself is new.

evidence.ref: maps-site/index.html :: The Beacon Post (2821); function pick(ar){return ar[Math.floor(R()*ar.length)];} (2170)

claims.text: Existing halt-like data: party-route stops JSTOPS (filled from JPATH waypoints), sea-lanes.json (4 lanes), sim caravan agents (kind 'caravan', the grainRelief/firstRoute chronicle lines) and W.routes = new Map(). No halt entity exists. A sim road record is only {pts, from, to, major}, and the other point features are W.cairns and bridges.

evidence.ref: maps-site/index.html :: JSTOPS=[]; JPATH.forEach (1306); maps-site/data/sea-lanes.json length 4; index.html :: W.routes = new Map() (3511), W.roads.push(rd) (3872), W.cairns = [] (3455)

claims.text: Data for blazed paths: named-ways.json has 2 entries, loaded by the atlas. traced-roads.json holds 46 polylines and nothing in maps-site/index.html references it. The sim's W.roads (pushed at index.html 1397, 1405, 3872, with a major flag) can enter the sheet through the transform inside the DEM window. Canon key: dotted = major roadways only, so blazed paths are invented minor ways and must never be drawn dotted.

evidence.ref: node JSON length of maps-site/data/{named-ways,traced-roads}.json = 2/46; grep traced-roads maps-site/index.html = no match; index.html :: W.roads.push

claims.text: Muster days anchor to the shipped POI 'The Muster Ground' ('A flat field where the levies drill badly and swear well.'). It is one of 5 civic picks that only town or capital plans draw (about 1 in 5 of those), so it is not guaranteed on any given sheet. Hazard sources in the sim: chron (3346), W.banditCamps (3458; push 5206), caravan ambush a.robbed (5225-5229), the Pebros camp chron (7239), W.dragon (3474) and its wake chron 'a dragon of the old brood, a child of Laegos' (5390). No notice schema with start, end or severity exists.

evidence.ref: maps-site/index.html :: The Muster Ground (2830); index.html :: W.dragon = (3474), W.banditCamps (3458), a dragon of the old brood (5390)

claims.text: The sim's eclipse is not a daily dark-hour schedule. W.eclipseUntil = performance.now() + 20000 is set by a random omen (pick among comet/eclipse/redmoon/calf), and it uses a wall-clock duration. grep finds no 'dark hour' in index.html. Tamar's daily dark hour as a muster-day or shut-way window therefore has to be stated from canon, not read from a sim snapshot (R13 forbids wall-clock sources).

evidence.ref: index.html :: W.eclipseUntil = performance.now() + 20000 (5328); grep -niE 'dark hour' index.html = no match

claims.text: Data for shut ways: s.plagueFlag (set at 5140), famine chronicle prose (famineDeep, 3401), ambush a.robbed and the Pebros camp. Roads carry no status field and there is no detour model. The swap follows R12: the notices file or param, one committed sample snapshot, no mid-cycle pushes.

evidence.ref: index.html :: s.plagueFlag = true (5140), famineDeep (3401), W.roads.push rd={pts,from,to,major} (3871-3872); docs/filigree/README.md#R12

claims.text: Colour base and relief: the modern pyramid is the base. Relief comes from EPESHU_HF (const EPESHU_HF_URI, index.html 7584) via atlas = (1060,1240) + (g+0.5)·800/768. Check: Aldorūs at grid 373,276 maps to 1449.06,1528.02, inside sheet one 1216,1376,1760,1664. Outside the window [1060,1240]..[1860,2040] there is no DEM. Fixture F12 (cell 83,6, bbox 2656,192,2688,224) lies outside it, so the bible states the no-DEM rule there and no relief is invented (R22).

Tithe renames to flag (R10): maps-site/index.html still ships {n:'The Tithe-Yard', d:'…where the harvest-tithe is weighed…'} at 2820 (in the 'odd' pool beside The Beacon Post) and {n:'The Tithe-Barn'} at 2829 (in the civic pool beside The Muster Ground; its d: string has no 'tithe'). Today grep -oi tithe gives 3 hits on 2 lines (grep -ci = 2). A Job 3 unit renames them to 'The Tribute-Yard' / 'The Tribute-Barn' and changes 'harvest-tithe' to 'harvest-tribute', after which grep -ci tithe must be 0 (Job 4 F06). This is a rename, not a Job 1 gate failure.

evidence.ref: maps-site/index.html :: The Tithe-Yard (2820), harvest-tithe (2820), The Tithe-Barn (2829); grep -oi tithe maps-site/index.html | wc -l = 3; grep -ci = 2

claims.text: Reuse for toggling the stack: the Contents plates THEMES (whole/realms/roads/company) and DEFAULT_ON are the existing one-question-view mechanism. No filigree layer is in DEFAULT_ON, which fits R18 (the new layers ship default-off). The only new machinery the README allows is the FILIGREE block, the ATLAS.filigree hook, the default-off toggle and hash composition (U00), plus data files including a notices sample.

evidence.ref: maps-site/index.html :: var THEMES= (1157), var DEFAULT_ON= (1153); docs/filigree/README.md#7 'The only new machinery'

gaps: Which settlements on sheet one roll The Beacon Post or The Muster Ground in their genCityCanvas plans was not established (needs a browser run of the seeded generator per name).
What the sparse era-tile differences are (names, borders or retouching) was not inspected, so whether R14's 'old-name layer' condition holds is open.
Whether the war/imperial pyramids register pixel-exactly with modern for an opacity under-stack was not verified beyond identical z/x/y file sets.
No source for the daily schedule of Tamar's dark hour (time and length) was found in the sim or the read inputs; the canon wiki was not consulted.
No notice schema exists (start/end/severity/target way, detour geometry, file name); its shape is left to Job 2.
Whether lexicon etymology can supply older place-name forms for an old-name layer was not checked.
Swiss-side detail of the building register (per-building point rendering, licence) remains unverified per dossier finding 15.
summary: The seven Swiss layers map to base (colour base plus DEM relief), under (old survey) and over (every structure, caravan halts and blazed paths as static seeded sheets; muster days and shut ways as per-session notices per R12). Today the era control is a single-base swap with no hash. Halts, structures, paths and notices have no entities, so they reuse the shipped Beacon Post / Muster Ground POIs (in-town picks, ~1/8 and ~1/5) and sim hazards, and the sim eclipse is wall-clock rather than a daily dark hour. The Tithe-Yard (with 'harvest-tithe') and The Tithe-Barn (3 'tithe' hits on 2 lines) must be renamed to Tribute-Yard/Tribute-Barn by a Job 3 unit under R10.
